tagline: Measure your pages the way people see them, then fix what fails
use_when: A page looks cramped, empty, too small or broken on a phone, or you are about to call a page done and want proof it holds up on real screens.
promises: Nothing is built until you approve it
try_it: Use the visual-qa skill to check /pricing and /account at desktop and phone sizes and propose fixes for anything that fails.

features.label: Three Screen Sizes
features.sub: Every page is captured on two laptops and a phone
features.title: Every page is captured on two laptops and a phone
features.what: Each page is opened at 1440×900, 1280×800 and 390×844, the way a person would see it. A layout that only works on your own monitor gets caught.
features.html:
1440×900
1280×800
390×844

features.label: No Sideways Scroll
features.sub: Flags any page that scrolls sideways
features.title: Flags any page that scrolls sideways
features.what: A page that is wider than the screen fails, with the number of extra pixels. Wide tables are expected to scroll inside their own box instead of dragging the whole page.

features.label: Text You Can Read
features.sub: Flags text smaller than 16 px, even inside charts
features.title: Flags text smaller than 16 px, even inside charts
features.what: Every piece of visible text is measured, including chart labels at the size they actually render. The floor is 16 px by default, and you can raise it for an older audience.

features.label: Big Enough to Tap
features.sub: Buttons and links under 44 px get flagged
features.title: Buttons and links under 44 px get flagged
features.what: Every button, link and form field is checked for a 44 px tap area both ways. Links inside a sentence are left alone, since nobody expects those to be big.

features.label: Nothing Cut Off
features.sub: Catches text cut short while there's room beside it
features.title: Catches text cut short while there's room beside it
features.what: Titles that end in an ellipsis even though there is plenty of space next to them get flagged. You see the full name unless the screen truly has no room for it.

features.label: No Broken Words
features.sub: Catches words split in the middle across two lines
features.title: Catches words split in the middle across two lines
features.what: A name that breaks into "Wildflo" on one line and "wer" on the next gets flagged, along with the CSS fix. Long names with slashes get a clean break point after the slash instead.

features.label: How Much Fits
features.sub: Counts how many items fit on the first screen
features.title: Counts how many items fit on the first screen
features.what: On lists, tables and stores, it counts what you see before scrolling and how much space the header takes first. Targets like six list lines on a laptop and three on a phone turn "feels empty" into a number.

features.label: Uses the Screen
features.sub: Desktop content should fill at least 70% of the width
features.title: Desktop content should fill at least 70% of the width
features.what: A narrow column floating in a wide screen is flagged with how much of the width it uses. Content is expected to fill most of the screen, capped near 1200 px and centered.

features.label: Every State, Not Just One
features.sub: Full, empty, long text and missing values each get a look
features.title: Full, empty, long text and missing values each get a look
features.what: Each page is captured in every state a person can reach: full of data, empty, with very long names, with missing values, and as each kind of user. You list the pages and states in a small pages file (an example is bundled). The empty state is where layouts usually break.

features.sub: Sheets, dialogs and expanders are opened and measured
features.title: Sheets, dialogs and expanders are opened and measured
features.what: Anything that only appears after a click, like a slide-up sheet, a dialog or an expanding section, is opened the way a person would and measured as its own state.

features.label: Signed In for Real
features.sub: Signs in through your real form, password never shown
features.title: Signs in through your real form, password never shown
features.what: Pages behind a login are reached by signing in through the actual sign-in form, using a small sign-in hook you write (an example is bundled). The hook reads the password from an untracked env file and never prints it, and any secret on screen is blanked before the screenshot.

features.title: Tests with lifelike data, then restores what was there
features.what: Before capturing, the feature is filled with data shaped like real use: realistic counts, long names, blanks. The starting state is noted first and put back afterward.

features.title: Checks every page your change touches, not just one

features.what: Mockups use your page's own fonts, colors and data, and are drawn to show the target being met: a laptop frame that really holds eight lines, a phone frame with 16 px text and 44 px buttons.

features.what: Each review item's reason gives the measured number next to the target it missed. You decide on facts, not on how a page feels.

features.title: Choices that aren't layout fixes become questions
features.what: Anything that is really your decision, like whether to hide sold-out items, is asked as a question rather than quietly decided as part of a layout fix.

features.label: Where the Page Goes

features.title: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.what: Your project picks where review pages go: a private claude.ai link, an HTML file that opens in your browser, or that file served on your home Wi-Fi so a phone can open it. Nothing is ever uploaded or tunneled in the Wi-Fi mode, and the server stops when the review ends.
